evidence.body:
# Summary

The EU AI Act is Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, and it entered into force on 1 August 2024. A small SaaS company that only uses third-party AI APIs mostly acts as a deployer rather than a provider, so its duties are narrower than those of model vendors. The practical work is an inventory of where AI is used, a short internal policy, and a record of which provider supplies each model.

# Key findings

- When: the AI Act became applicable on 2 August 2026 with exceptions. Prohibited AI practices and AI literacy obligations entered into application from 2 February 2025, and the governance rules and the obligations for GPAI models became applicable on 2 August 2025.

- Fines: breaking the prohibited AI practices rules is subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or up to 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. Breaches of other operator obligations can reach EUR 15 000 000 or 3 %, and supplying incorrect information EUR 7 500 000 or 1 %. In the case of SMEs, including start-ups, each fine is whichever of the two amounts is lower.

- Duties: deployers of AI systems must take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff. When people use an AI system such as a chatbot, they should be made aware that they are interacting with a machine, and AI-generated content must be identifiable.

# Sources

1. Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Official Journal: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj
2. European Commission, regulatory framework and timeline: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai
3. AI Act Explorer, Article 99 (penalties): https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/99/
